A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CodeSteer research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SymBench evaluations, cross-model experiments, complexity analyses, component ablations, and token/runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of o1 augmented with CodeSteer, heuristic baselines, and unnormalized aggregate scores.

M1.justification: The CodeSteer guidance procedure, two checkers, SFT weighting, DPO scoring and sampling, and five-turn limit remain unchanged. Applying CodeSteer to o1 and renaming rounds as turns do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 37 SymBench tasks and retain the existing complexity scenarios. The new experiments select existing tasks and change evaluated model or comparator configurations without introducing new task requirements or domains.

E2.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix K add three evaluated comparators: Few-Shot, Code-First-Rule, and Code-First-Agent. These introduce direct comparisons against heuristic alternatives to learned steering on five tasks. The original Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds an o1-as-TaskLLM evaluation on five randomly selected unseen tasks and an unnormalized averaging check. The new heuristic comparisons specify five demonstration prompts and a code-first strategy using code for the first three rounds. Existing splits, sample counts, training settings, and execution limits are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5 and new Appendix I test sensitivity to the aggregation metric by recomputing scores without normalization. The existing component ablations, complexity curves, and illustrated cases remain unchanged, including the full ablation table moved from Appendix K to M.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the reported comparisons. The new tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 3 establishes gains from augmenting o1 itself, including Cryptanalysis success rising from 60% to 73% and Synthesis Decomposition from 57% to 94%. Table 9 adds heuristic comparisons, such as Game 24 scores of 93% for CodeSteer versus 28%, 68%, and 76%. Table 7 adds raw averages, including 75.2% overall for CodeSteer versus 72.3% for o1. These extend the empirical findings; existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The recursive DPO score in Equation 1 and normalized evaluation score in Equation 2 are unchanged. v2 adds no theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same central contributions and headline claims, including the 53.3-to-86.4 GPT-4o improvement and cross-model transfer claim. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds explanations involving problem-specific algorithm guidance and code refining partial textual solutions. Section 8 newly identifies insufficient TaskLLM capability, inefficient code causing timeouts, and incorrect code/text choices at intermediate complexity as failure conditions. These qualify the retained conclusions.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a Hugging Face resource-access link alongside the existing GitHub link. Section 5.5 documents the new heuristic procedures, while the original prompts, checker code, dataset counts, hyperparameters, and hardware information in Appendices D–H remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Ai et al. (2025) ResMoE citation in the related-work discussion of reasoning-model resource costs. Other reference changes primarily update existing works' publication metadata; the overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 generally replaces round terminology with turn, adds Sections 5.4–5.5, a limitations passage and acknowledgments, and expands the appendix contents. Most existing prose and the overall section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables for o1 augmentation, unnormalized scores, and heuristic comparisons. Existing tables are renumbered, Figure 4 moves, and surrounding content reflows. All 12 figure images are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The o1 and heuristic comparisons provide useful additional validation, while Appendix I shows that the aggregate advantage survives removing normalization. The new limitations make applicability clearer. These are focused improvements to the existing empirical case, with the method and original results preserved; the new comparisons remain limited to five-task subsets.
